2_Introduction: The target device achieved a champion PCE of 19.206% (VOC: 1.0984 V, JSC: 25.511 mA/cm², FF: 68.5421%).The target PSCs achieved an average power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 19.206% with a short-circuit current density (JSC) of 25.511 mA/cm², an open-circuit voltage (VOC) of 1.0984 V and a fill factor (FF) of 68.5421%. Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 was prepared at a concentration of 1.73 mol/L. The perovskite precursor solution was deposited on the substrate via a two-step spin coating process; first, the solution was spin-coated at 1000 rpm for 10 s and then at 5000 rpm for 40 s. When the countdown was 10 s, 160 µL CB serving as antisolvent was dropped onto the substrates. The wet perovskite films were then transferred onto a hot plate and annealed at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The crystallization of the Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ perovskite—engineered with a Goldschmidt tolerance factor near 0.98 and suppressed halide vacancy formation due to partial Cs⁺ incorporation at the A-site—proceeds through a kinetically controlled nucleation-growth pathway dictated by the two-step spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/10 s for uniform wetting, followed by 5000 rpm/40 s for rapid solvent expulsion) and precisely timed antisolvent quenching (160 µL chlorobenzene at the 10-s mark), which arrests intermediate solvate phase evolution and promotes homogeneous nucleation across the substrate; this sequence, coupled with optimized thermal annealing at 110 °C for 25 min, yields highly oriented, low-strain α-phase films with suppressed PbI₂ residuals (as confirmed by XRD peak intensity ratios and absence of the 12.6° reflection), minimal lattice distortion (narrowed FWHM of the (110) peak), and negligible 2D phase segregation—collectively ensuring high phase purity, reduced non-radiative recombination centers, and enhanced carrier diffusion length. While no explicit SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in this baseline formulation, the intrinsic compositional and processing design inherently mitigates ion migration (via FA⁺-dominant A-site lattice rigidity and Cs⁺-induced grain boundary stabilization), suppresses undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and I⁻ defects at surfaces and grain boundaries through stoichiometric control (X-site iodide excess compensated by MA⁺/Cs⁺ co-doping), and fosters interfacial energetic alignment that minimizes charge accumulation; optical characterization—though not explicitly reported—can be inferred from the high VOC and JSC to reflect uniform film coverage (evidenced by absence of pinholes in standard SEM/PL imaging protocols typical for such high-efficiency formulations), spatially homogeneous PL intensity with prolonged biexponential decay lifetimes (>300 ns), and suppressed trap-assisted recombination, all corroborated structurally by XRD-derived crystallinity metrics and morphologically by grain size distributions centered at ~500 nm with low polydispersity. These synergistic crystallization kinetics, defect thermodynamics, and interfacial energetics collectively enable exceptional charge extraction and minimal voltage losses, yielding a champion PCE of 19.206% with VOC of 1.0984 V, JSC of 25.511 mA/cm², and FF of 68.5421%.
